items.label: of demand growth met by solar
renewables' share of generation
items.note: Coal 33.0%. The IEA sees them level

notes: Solar generation rose from 2143 TWh in 2024 to 2778 TWh, up 636 TWh or 30%, enough to meet 75% of demand growth on its own. Wind and solar together met 99%. Solar overtook wind (2715 TWh) for the first time. The IEA puts the solar increase lower: 620 TWh in Electricity 2026 and about 600 TWh in the Global Energy Review 2026. Only Ember says renewables have overtaken coal, at 33.8% against 33.0%. The IEA has both at about 34%, roughly level, and in its July mid-year update expects renewables to pull clearly ahead in 2026.
